title: First motion comes from the soul; the heavens cannot rest
pass_a_gloss: Whence does the body have motion, if not from the soul? For the body is not self-moving. Those who want to show a first genesis of motion from the elements by lightness and heaviness show a second cause, not a first. It is false that the elements move themselves by being light or heavy by nature: if lightness and heaviness were motion, the light and heavy would never stop; yet they stop when they reach their proper place. Even if that were granted, how could reasoning, opining, and judging be works of lightness and heaviness? And the cosmos, sun, and moon, moving by nature, cannot rest by nature. In the same way the soul, ever-moving by nature, cannot rest by nature; for rest is corruption of the soul and of every ever-moving thing.
pass_b_english: Where does the body's motion come from, if not the soul? The body is not a self-mover. Appeals to elemental lightness and heaviness do not give a first beginning of motion; they give a later account. Light and heavy things do come to rest in their places — so those qualities are not perpetual motion itself. Still less can thinking, judging, and forming opinions be the work of weight. The world, the sun, and the moon move by nature and cannot naturally stand still. So too the soul: by nature it is always in motion, and natural rest would be its undoing.
